anya: Heads-up — bringing up atlas-28k (28k context variant) in int4X. After warm-prefill + streaming we see a deterministic drift starting ~8.1k tokens: int4 output diverges from fp16 baseline. Repro below.

mike_ml: can you paste a minimal repro? deterministic across seeds?

anya: repro (short):
```
# reproduce locally
python tests/repro_stream.py --model atlas-28k-int4x --prompt \"<long multi-paragraph prompt>\" --stream-chunk-size 512 --seed 42

# observed (truncated)
# fp16: \"...the conference will be held in Boston in June...\"
# int4x: \"...thè conference will be held in Boston in June...\"
```

brian: hmm looks like a KV index/slot skew. checksum mismatch at a cache boundary often indicates an off-by-one in the streaming prefill/append path :thinking:

anya: i ran `tools/kv-checksum --model atlas-28k-int4x --session 20260321-1` and got:
kv checksum diverged at token_idx=8192, shard=2, layer=18
sha1(fp16_kv)=a1b2c3d4e5f6deadbeef
sha1(int4x_kv)=a1b2c3d4e5f6deadde0f

carmen: quick hypothesis — rotary scaling table is produced during fp16 compile. the int4 execution path uses a packed layout and i suspect a reshape/stride miscompute when we memcpy into the cached buffer. try forcing rot rescale at runtime or build with ROPE_KEEP_FP=true to confirm.

anya: running with `--force-rot-rescale=true` + rebuild with ROPE_KEEP_FP=true now. i'll rerun checksum and post results. if it fixes, i'll open a CR and tag @eng-runtime + @eng-ml. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created issue ENG-7892: \"atlas-28k int4x: KV index skew at 8192 boundary\" and assigned to @eng-runtime
